+# https://www.irishstatutebook.ie/eli/1947/sro/71/made/en/print
+
+# From Stan Ulbrych (2026-09-12):
+# Ireland's Summer Time Act, 1925 (No. 8 of 1925, see above)
+# ended summer time at 02:00 GMT on the day after the third Saturday in
+# September, that is, 1925-09-20. The UK's Summer Time Act, 1925, however,
+# moved the UK's end date to the day after the first Saturday in October with
+# immediate effect, but it did not apply to the Irish Free State.
+# Ireland matched the October date only from 1926, via the Summer Time Order,
+# 1926, whose recital replaces the period fixed by section 2 of the 1925 Act
+# and mentions no earlier order. Moving approval of that order in the
+# Dáil on 1926-03-24, Minister Kevin O'Higgins said:
+#
+#     Deputies will remember that last year there was a discrepancy of a
+#     fortnight between the termination of Summer Time in the Saorstát and
+#     in Great Britain and Northern Ireland.  As a result of that, serious
+#     inconvenience was caused to railway companies, and there was a certain
+#     amount of dislocation of postal services in the country.
+#
+# (See: https://www.oireachtas.ie/en/debates/debate/dail/1926-03-24/18/)
+# So Dublin fell back on 1925-09-20, two weeks before London.

@@ -1772,1 +1772,30 @@
-# For Atikokan see America/Panama.
+# From Tim Parenti (2026-09-21), per Paul Eggert (2000-10-02, 2006-07-17):
+# In the northwest of the province, most portions of Kenora, Rainy River, and
+# Thunder Bay Districts lying broadly west of 90°W longitude have historically
+# been aligned with neighboring Manitoba and use America/Winnipeg, in
+# accordance with section 2(2) of Ontario's Time Act, RSO 1990 chapter T.9:
+# https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90t09
+# With Manitoba now opting to stay on -05 year-round, if any of these areas do
+# not follow, it would require a new zone; however, given the short leadtime
+# ahead of a potential divergence on 2026-11-01 and in the interest of not
+# creating zones that may not be needed, assume for the time being that they
+# will.
+#
+# In practice, there are several exceptions to the 90°W dividing line set by
+# the province, all of which technically contravene the official Ontario rules:
+#   - An area around Big Trout Lake in Kenora District observes Central Time
+#     (-06/-05) despite extending east of 90°W.
+#   - An area around Upsala in the southwest of Thunder Bay District observes
+#     Eastern Time (-05/-04) like America/Toronto despite extending west of
+#     90°W.
+#   - Atikokan in the east of Rainy River District has observed year-round -05
+#     (EST) since at least 1952; this matches America/Panama since our 1970
+#     cutoff.
+#   - Pickle Lake and the Mishkeegogamang First Nation (formerly New Osnaburgh)
+#     in Kenora District have also observed year-round -05 (EST) since at least
+#     1998, though it is less clear how far back that arrangement goes; assume
+#     the area is covered in the same way as Atikokan.
+# See the 'backzone' file for further commentary.
+# At time of writing, it is not yet known to what extent Manitoba's 2026-09-17
+# announcement may spur further adaptations in northwestern Ontario; see
+# Manitoba, below.
@@ -1807,0 +1836,34 @@
+# From Tim Parenti (2026-09-29):
+# As much of western Canada began announcing year-round DST in early 2026,
+# Manitoba Premier Wab Kinew publicly mused on forming a "Prairie time zone" by
+# joining Saskatchewan and Alberta on year-round -06, while committing to
+# conducting a public engagement survey on the matter.  The results, however,
+# showed that while "[a] total of 92 per cent of Manitobans surveyed wanted to
+# see an end to seasonal time changes", "[a] majority of Manitobans (58 per
+# cent) preferred to stay on permanent DST, while 34 per cent voted to
+# eliminate the time change but stay on standard time."
+#
+# The survey results were published on Thursday 2026-09-17 alongside a policy
+# announcement adopting permanent DST, or year-round -05, just over 6 weeks
+# before clocks would otherwise fall back on 2026-11-01.
+# https://news.gov.mb.ca/news/?item=75397
+# https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/manitoba/daylight-time-manitoba-9.7347844
+#
+# While other potential options would have required further legislation, the
+# Official Time Amendment Act (Bill 2 of the 42nd Legislature's 5th Session),
+# assented to 2023-05-30, provides for year-round -05 upon proclamation.
+# https://web2.gov.mb.ca/laws/statutes/2023/pdf/c00423.pdf
+# Order in Council 221/2026, issued 2026-09-23, directed the proclamation
+# bringing the Act into force on 2026-10-31, 26 hours before clocks would
+# otherwise fall back.
+# https://oic.gov.mb.ca/OICDocs/2026/09/Municipal%20and%20Northern%20Relations.260923.%20Official%20Time%20Amendment%20Act.2212026.pdf
+# https://web2.gov.mb.ca/laws/statutes/proclamations/2023c4(2026-10-31).pdf
+#
+# The Act further allows for the Lieutenant Governor in Council to, on
+# recommendation of the relevant minister, "make regulations varying the
+# reckoning" of official time in Manitoba, provided the minister has "due
+# regard for the applicable time zone in neighbouring jurisdictions."
+#
+# Use a temporary hack like Alberta’s to work around potential CLDR
+# limitations.
+

@@ -2124,12 +2197,17 @@
-# From Tim Parenti (2026-09-10):
-# Although on 2026-09-01 the Town of Golden voted instead to split its
-# timekeeping practice from RDEK and rejoin BC on year-round -07, this was met
-# with significant pushback from residents in Golden and CSRD Area A.  In light
-# of these public comments, CSRD voted on 2026-09-10 to defer its decision on
-# timekeeping in Area A “to gather and assess further information before a
-# decision is implemented”.  As such, at time of writing, it seems likely that
-# Golden may soon revisit its decision as well.
-#
-# For now, these areas remain aligned with America/Edmonton, but if they
-# diverge, a new zone with a name like 'America/Brit_Columbia/Golden' would be
-# needed.
+# From Tim Parenti (2026-09-24):
+# Echoing RDEK’s earlier false step, the Town of Golden initially opted for
+# year-round -07 by a 4–2 Council vote on 2026-09-01.  This was met with
+# significant pushback from residents preferring to maintain the existing
+# alignment with RDEK and Alberta, with a formal petition swiftly gathering
+# 2,395 signatures in two weeks from the town of 3,986 and some smaller
+# neighboring communities.  In response, Council unanimously rescinded the
+# resolution at the following meeting on 2026-09-22, and unanimously replaced
+# it with year-round -06 to keep the regional alignment.
+# Acknowledging that “its initial move was driven in part by concerns about
+# dark winter mornings and pedestrian safety for children travelling to
+# school”, the new resolution directs town staff to partner on safety supports
+# and commits to reviewing the decision and its impacts in October 2027.
+# https://www.ctvnews.ca/calgary/article/golden-bc-council-reverses-course-on-time-zone-opts-for-mountain-daylight-time/
+# At time of writing, the surrounding CSRD Area A is yet to formalize its own
+# decision following a 2026-09-10 deferral “to gather and assess further
+# information”, but is expected to follow.
